title: Scalable Graph Condensation with Evolving Capabilities

problem.claim: The rapid growth and evolving nature of graph data create scalability and updating challenges for graph algorithms and graph condensation.

gap.claim: Existing graph condensation approaches assume a static training set and therefore do not efficiently handle growing or streaming graph data.

contributions.claim: GECC is a scalable graph condensation method for large-scale and evolving graph data.
GECC performs class-wise clustering on aggregated features and inherits previous condensation results as clustering centroids when the condensed graph expands.
The framework enables efficient updates to a distilled graph for data streams without costly retraining.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present a novel framework for continual graph condensation with evolving capabilities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report robust theoretical foundations for the methodology.
The authors report that GECC outperforms most state-of-the-art graph condensation methods in comprehensive experiments including a real-world scenario.
The authors report an around 1000× speedup on large datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph growth creates major scalability challenges, and graph condensation addresses them by learning a small graph for downstream tasks.
Existing condensation methods assume static training data, creating inefficiencies for dynamic and growing graph data.
The work introduces continual graph condensation and the GECC method for efficient updates on evolving graph data.
GECC uses class-wise clustering on aggregated features and reuses prior condensation results as centroids when expanding the condensed graph.
The authors report theoretical support, improved performance over most state-of-the-art methods, and an around 1000× speedup on large datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical results or assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the downstream tasks, datasets, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the data-stream model or update algorithm in detail.
